stories.title: Eastern Ukraine frontline
stories.summary: The eastern front around Donetsk and the broader Donbas remains highly attritional since the start of the full-scale war in 2022. Both sides use drone strikes, artillery, and manpower in attempts to translate localized gains into operational momentum. Observers watch for shifts in tempo, fortifications, and the ability to sustain pressure without a decisive breakthrough. The risk remains that stalemate persists as both sides accrue casualties and material losses.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: The live angle centers on whether ongoing pressure can convert localized advances into an operational shift.

stories.title: Southern Ukraine fighting
stories.summary: Southern Ukraine continues as a strategic, static front toward the land corridor to Crimea. The focus is on whether strikes, fortifications, and logistics pressure around Zaporizhzhia and the lower Dnipro can alter the balance, even without sweeping maneuvers. The region remains vital for supply lines and regional military posture, with civilian impacts shaping the public narrative.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Recent assessments consider whether logistical pressure changes balance around Zaporizhzhia.

stories.title: Gaza fighting
stories.summary: Gaza stands as the densest urban-war marker in the region, with civilian movement, aid access, hostage diplomacy, and ceasefire negotiations shaping headlines. While linked to broader Iran-Israel dynamics, the local story hinges on operational shifts from raids to a potential durable political arrangement. Civilians face escalating humanitarian challenges amid ongoing security operations.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Diplomacy continues over hostage and ceasefire terms in the Gaza context.

stories.title: South Lebanon strikes
stories.summary: South Lebanon serves as a pressure gauge for a wider Israel-Hezbollah confrontation. The daily pattern is a cycle of strikes, evacuations, rocket exchanges, and deterrence signaling rather than a conventional invasion. The risk of escalation grows if misreadings occur, potentially widening regional tensions and impacting civilian areas.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: The front remains a cycle of strikes and deterrence signaling with potential for wider escalation.

stories.title: Red Sea / Yemen attacks
stories.summary: The Red Sea/Yemen marker tracks Houthi missile and drone activity affecting shipping and military responses around Bab el-Mandeb. The central question is whether attacks and associated insurance costs deter vessels from Suez despite fluctuating headline attention. Security operators monitor shipping routes and countermeasures in the broader Yemen conflict.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Houthi attacks and shipping security remain the focal point for maritime risk in the region.

stories.title: Khartoum fighting
stories.summary: Khartoum has become a fragmented urban battlefield amid Sudan’s army-RSF conflict and a governance crisis. The current signal is whether control shifts in the capital translate into improved aid access or simply relocate fighting and displacement. The humanitarian situation is increasingly precarious as clashes fragment cities and threaten essential services.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Control dynamics in Khartoum will influence aid access and displacement patterns.

stories.title: Darfur fighting
stories.summary: Darfur presents the most worrying Sudanese spillover, with local violence and displacement intersecting with cross-border routes into Chad. The live angle centers on whether pressure around El Fasher and surrounding corridors worsens the humanitarian emergency and regional stability. Cross-border dynamics remain a critical factor for security and aid delivery.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Worsening humanitarian conditions around El Fasher are a key concern.

stories.title: Sahel insurgency belt
stories.summary: The Sahel tri-border zone remains an insurgency belt across Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, with cross-border militant mobility amplified by external influence. Recent coordinated attacks highlight that junta legitimacy, external support, and regional security are closely intertwined, affecting civilian safety and governance legitimacy in multiple states.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Coordinated attacks in Mali underscore the region’s multifaceted security challenges.

stories.title: Lake Chad / Boko Haram activity
stories.summary: Lake Chad continues as a regional insurgency system affecting Nigeria, Niger, Cameroon, and Chad through raids, displacement, and fragile border communities. The battle lines are fluid, with ongoing concerns about civilian protection and the ability of governments to secure multi-country border areas against Boko Haram and IS-linked groups.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Cross-border insurgent activity continues to challenge regional stability.

stories.title: Far North Cameroon violence
stories.summary: Far North Cameroon is tied to the Lake Chad insurgency ecosystem, though events are often smaller than headlines from Nigeria. The strategic issue centers on border insecurity and civilian vulnerability in a region with limited state reach, requiring sustained humanitarian and security attention.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Border-region insecurity persists with civilian vulnerability in focus.

stories.title: Sagaing / Myanmar fighting
stories.summary: Sagaing remains a core resistance-war zone in Myanmar’s post-coup conflict, with anti-junta forces seeking to hold territory and disrupt logistics while civilians face airstrikes, displacement, and governance fragmentation. The front line’s resilience or breakdown will influence broader national dynamics and humanitarian needs.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Anti-junta forces aim to hold territory to disrupt military logistics.

stories.title: Eastern DRC / Kivu clashes
stories.summary: Eastern DRC and Kivu areas remain shaped by M23 activity, Congolese forces, and regional involvement, with continued civilian displacement and contested control of roads and mining sites. The diplomatic ceasefire language versus on-the-ground realities remains a key dynamic, as armed groups retain leverage in strategic corridors.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Ceasefire rhetoric competes with persistent armed control of routes.

stories.title: Kashmir militarized zone
stories.summary: Kashmir remains a militarized India-Pakistan border zone where local attacks, arrests, and cross-border fire can trigger crisis diplomacy between nuclear-armed states. The live signal is whether any incident alters troop postures, air restrictions, or border measures, with civilians remaining at risk in the affected districts.

stories.title: What to watch
stories.summary: Any incident could shift troop posture and border restrictions.
